There is no work by Haydn called "Sunrise Symphony". His “Sunrise” work is the String Quartet in B-flat major, Op. 76, No. 4.
His Symphony No. 6 is conventionally called Le matin (“Morning”). Its opening depicts a sunrise, which may explain references to it as a “sunrise symphony,” but that is not its standard nickname.
There is a work specifically titled "Sunrise Symphony", but it is Calvin Taylor, not Haydn. It’s a five-movement work for orchestra and chorus.

I think what bothered me most about this puzzle--other than the 33% germination rate, which seems rather low--is the {pea}.

Now "beet" is a singular noun--one beet, two beets, three beets. But an average sized beet is pretty big--you could make, if not a meal, a side dish from it. And "corn" and "kale," as commonly used, are uncountable--an ear of corn, a bunch of kale.

But a pea? What the heck am supposed to do with one pea?
